quest.title: The Gardener
quest.description: Following the principles of "truth," people gain knowledge, learn of boundaries, and nurture reverence. This mindset provides a safe borderline — while also shackling the mad.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x875, Primogem x60, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, have you ever wondered why Albedo always keeps his office closed? Paimon bets there's a secret snack stash hidden around here somewh—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waaaaaah!

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: Hey! Not so loud!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: M—Mini Durin!? What are you doing here!?

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: Well, um... Actually...

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: I've kind of been helping you guys in secret this whole time. I tried tapping Paimon on the shoulder during the battle, but you floated away too fast...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You were there?

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: Yeah. I've been in Mondstadt for a few days now, but I've kept myself out of sight. I thought people might be scared of me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry! We aren't scared of you!

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: Hehe... Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what brings you here? Ooh, is it Windblume? There are a ton of fun games this time of year...

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: I did sneak off to the festival for a bit! Even though I couldn't play the games because of all the people, I still had a lot of fun!

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: But, that's not why I'm here. Albedo and I made a promise to accomplish something great together.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean...?

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: I... I'm gonna replace the Durin on Dragonspine. I'm gonna be the one who is revived and brought into this world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, didn't that already happen? You left the storybook world, and now you're here...

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: Sorry, sorry. I should be more specific...

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: Albedo said he can use alchemy to turn me into a human.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Human transmutation... So, you're Albedo's intended subject.

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: Yeah. He's been working on it for a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And that's what you want, Mini Durin? To become human?

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: I don't know if "want" is the right word... I don't even know if there's a right answer in a situation like this.

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: B—But, I do know this — I have just as much of a right to this name. I don't want to lose to the other Durin.

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: I know. Albedo talked to me about that. He said the Durin on Dragonspine is a lot more aggressive and primitive. Almost like... a beast.

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: But, mom created me in a storybook. The pure parts of me can balance out the evil parts of him.

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: If I'm honest, I don't know what that will look like — if I can still be "me" once I become one with that part of him.

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: Maybe, without a complete soul, there was never really a "me" to begin with... Albedo said these kinds of questions are normal. We're all just trying to figure out who we are.

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: But, I'm not afraid of change. I want my life to have meaning, and suppressing an evil dragon, becoming human... Both sound pretty meaningful to me.

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: So, don't worry. No one is forcing me to make this choice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, turning you into a human sounds like a huge project!

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: ...Yeah, I'm really grateful to him. We're kind of in the same boat, y'know?

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: Albedo told me he's the "Kreideprinz," a synthetic human. And if this works, I'll be one too.

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: We will be the only two of our kind in the whole world — alchemical creations allowed to live in human form.

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: If all living things are grouped together by "species," and there's only one other person like me in this world, I guess that makes us... family.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Definitely! You've just got to trust one another.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, while we're on the subject, does your friend Hat Guy know about this?

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: Yeah. I told him I was coming here to fulfill this, um... duty. He didn't try to stop me, just told me to "get a move on then."

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: He didn't say it outright, but I think he supports my decision. Maybe he even thinks it's a good idea to go through with this.

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: ...I'm a little scared, of course. But excited, too!

response.speaker: Mini Durin
response.text: Anyway, I'm really glad I got to talk to you at a time like this. I feel a lot better now, so thanks!

choices.text: Isn't as simple as just changing form.

talks.objective: Go to the location indicated by Alice

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We did it!

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Yes, very well done.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Aw, they've grown up so fast... I'm so proud.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Really? Well, then I'll leave you to debrief the others about today's events.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Huh? You're leaving already?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: You did marvelously today — I'm thrilled for both of you. And should you feel the need to gloat profusely to that student of mine so she knows to up her game, be my guest! Hahahaha.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Lovely tea party, but that'll do me for now. Until next time, my dearies.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: You're just going to up and leave? Barbie!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: You'll have to forgive Barbeloth — she's always on the move. And she never says where she's going either. I think she enjoys the mystique.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: But if I had to guess, she's probably going for a walk. Hehe, she's a very health-conscious individual.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Barbie was satisfied with your victory, and so am I. Congratulations to you both.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: You can come back now! ...Oh, whoops, I need to turn you back to normal first, don't I...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Welcome, one and all. Please sit wherever you like.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: So, no unspoken rules to be aware of? I don't wanna unwittingly park myself down on some important lady's chair...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: I highly doubt anyone's going to mind where you sit, Lord Barbatos. But thank you for being so considerate.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Jean didn't fancy tagging along?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: A lot happened in the city today. If she left, there really would be no one around to lead the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Alright, never mind. I was just hoping to treat her to some tea. *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: So tell me, Albedo, what is this outrageous and audacious plan of yours that I've been hearing murmurings about?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'll get right to the point.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I intend to kill the evil Durin in Dragonspine.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Oh?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: And I'd also like to request some alchemical reagents from the Hexenzirkel.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Which ones? I'm all ears.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: First would be the flesh of that immortal monster from the Mare Jivari.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Interesting... What else?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The other is a portion of the "embryo" left by my mother, Rhinedottir.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Ah, the raw material from which she created her monsters in the past... There's not much of it left.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Dragon blood, monster flesh, and embryo... Sounds to me like a formula for creating life?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Correct.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Durin's heart has continued to beat ever since the day he died. That means, it's just a matter of time before he eventually returns — it could be centuries away, or millennia, but the day will come.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I've spent years investigating in Dragonspine, so I'm well aware of the danger he poses.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: He has already posed a considerable threat to Mondstadt at less than half of his original strength... There's no telling how dire the consequences could be if he ever regained his full life force.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hence, if we want to be free of the dangers posed by his blood and limitless vitality, we must find a way to eliminate Durin entirely.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, Durin is a special entity. Even after death, he could reawaken at any moment.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: So, the solution is to kill him and then resurrect him in a different form.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Upon resurrection, he will no longer be the creature he once was. In fact, he will no longer be a monster at all, because I intend to transform him into a human-like being.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: During the summer, Klee and I visited a fairytale world called Simulanka. It was created by mages from the Hexenzirkel, so I'm sure you know of it.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Of course. It was even the home of one of M's children, the other Dur—... Ah, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It was during that journey that I learned, with certainty, that Durin would return to life one day.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: That experience inspired me. I met the pure soul M had created, and I knew if I wanted to change Durin's fate, he could be the key.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: To that end, I devised an alchemical model for the transmutation. The soul will come from the fairytale dragon of Simulanka, the blood from the original dragon's heart...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: And the monster remnants from the Mare Jivari and the embryo mother left behind will form the flesh.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The corrosive nature of the dragon venom and the heightened vitality of the monster remnants will offset each other, keeping the constructed body in perfect balance.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: A powerful side effect can be triggered when festering forces and life energy collide. In an alchemical setting, the results are sure to be nothing short of astounding.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: The glint in your eye when you talk about these ideas... you really are your mother's child.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Do you see that as a bad thing, Aunt Alice?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Of course not. To me, you're both extraordinary individuals. I find you fascinating.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: In any case, now I see why you asked Venti for help. The raw materials you seek are extremely valuable. The misuse of even the tiniest amount could cause unimaginable chaos.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: That said, we're happy to give you what you need, but there is one condition. You need to prove you can wield them, and so you must pass the Hexenzirkel's trial.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: #I understand. I figured something like this might happen. That's why I asked {NICKNAME} to come along.

choices.text: Wait, I'm joining you in this thing?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Haha, I can think of no better partner for such an endeavor.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Hm, so you know our tricks, huh...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Aunt Alice has always loved a spectacle — any chance to witness friends come together to support one another.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Well, success means little if you have no one to celebrate it with, no?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Although, I'm afraid dear Paimon will have to sit this one out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Why?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: The Hexenzirkel trials are no walk in the park, my dear. Besides, I already decided on the structure.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: There's only room for two participants, I'm afraid. No more no less... You understand, don't you, Paimon? Don't be too angry with your dear Aunt...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, okay, you can turn off the charm... Paimon will stay behind.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Hahaha, thank you for being so understanding. Then, whenever you two are ready, interact with the chessboard on the table — it will guide you through the trial.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: #Are you ready, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just about.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Then let me make a formal request. Will you go through this trial with me?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Then, my dear children, get ready for a taste of the Dodo-King's magic.

choices.text: You're not even gonna try to talk me into it?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Oh? You need convincing? I thought you'd want to keep an eye on me. Who knows what sort of... outlandish things I might attempt without someone to keep me in check.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Fine. I'm not going to argue with you.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's certainly in keeping with Hexenzirkel modalities.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've been shrunken down to chess-piece size.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, you're so tiny now! Take extra care of yourselves, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Pfft.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nothing. It's just... Paimon's voice is even louder than usual now I'm this size.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She's always so energetic and lively. Nothing can dampen her spirits.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Don't worry. You'll be back with her again in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: You sound pretty confident, Albedo.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Aunt Alice? I didn't realize you'd be personally conducting the trial.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Well, since your mother has to recuse herself, who better than I to put your abilities to the test?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: I have prepared quite a riveting new performance, just for you two. See?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Defeat them in battle. Prove to me that you have what it takes to achieve your goal.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Swashbuckle your way to victory, like gallant fairytale heroes.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: You did so much for us this time, Lord Barbatos. I don't even know how to thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Don't thank me at all, please. It makes it seem like I'm useless the rest of the time haha...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: You know that's not what I meant... An Archon has their own calculations. Who am I to question their wisdom?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Okay, now you give me too much credit. I admit, I'm not the most, um... proactive Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: You have your own hard work to thank for this result. Oh, and our friends the Honorary Knight and Paimon, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ah, worried about Albedo's plan?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I can't help it.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I have full confidence in his abilities. It's just an instinctual response.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: But, in the end, if he sets his mind to something, I know he will succeed. I trust him.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Haha, that's good to hear.

talks.objective: Return to normal and talk to Alice
Return to normal and talk to Alice

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're finally back! Great job. You made it all look so easy.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Nice to have you back safe and sound. Now, time to relax and switch off — you've earned it.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Felt pretty good to beat the trial.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Once you've rested up, let me know when you're free, and we'll head to Dragonspine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: To deal with the dragon of Dragonspine, right?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Indeed. The sooner we deal with Durin, the better.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: ...We've arrived. Sorry, Paimon, I have to get to work now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still beating away after all this time...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Leave it to me. You two, stay on guard.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Albedo's drawing a magic array... He's silent. Must be a solemn affair.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, may Paimon ask a question?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You may.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who is Durin to you? Do you think of him as... one of your kind? And is he a dragon, person, animal? Or... monster?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: From an alchemical perspective, we're both artificial creations, but biologically speaking, we have no relation whatsoever. So, to say we are kin would be categorically incorrect.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like you prefer humans to dragons, then?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's not so much a matter of preference. Rather, as things stand, I would say I belong to the class of "human." Albeit a unique category thereof — but then again, most forms of life in this world possess some unique traits.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I am perhaps the most unique among humans, in that I'm the only one of my kind. But soon there will be another just like me, assuming this alchemical project proves successful.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I believe Mini Durin already told you of his intent to replace the Durin of Dragonspine. After my conversation with him, he also expressed a strong interest in becoming human.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's a fascinating prospect, not to mention an extremely challenging one. But I understand why he came to that decision.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you see this as an act of "creation"?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Well... Understood in the broadest sense, this project deals with both the past and future, and stands to profoundly impact many lives. That, primarily, is what makes it worthwhile.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Helping Mini Durin become who he wants to be is a secondary consideration, though still a meaningful one.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: By contrast, my personal motivations are nothing so grand and meaningful. I'm just pursuing something I believe in.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: In my view, to cultivate life which the world cannot generate endogenously is to cultivate the world itself.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Whatever aids life in attaining a greater level of perfection improves the world by doing so.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It is not a question of whether this "ought" to be done or not, merely whether I wish to. The alchemical enterprise is concerned with deciphering and comprehending all forms of knowledge — that is the path I walk.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Of course, that's not to say that this is just a science experiment to me. Anything that affects Mondstadt, I approach first and foremost as a member of the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Does that answer your question satisfactorily?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well enough. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: ...Finished.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like a golden energy has encased the dragon's heart...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The whole heart would be too big — I don't need that much. Instead, I've just removed the core. The rest will soon lose its vitality completely.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: This time, Durin's body should finally die for good.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but in that case, what's gonna happen to the fake Hertha? And what about the people who fell under Durin's influence?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The Knights will keep an eye on them. But as far as I'm concerned, eliminating Durin's influence on the citizenry and creating a new Durin through alchemy are one and the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Armed with this heart, I'll be able to complete the alchemical array, and deal with all these issues in one go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Albedo, how did everything go?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Very smoothly, I'd say. We achieved our goal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? So... Mini Durin looks like a human now?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Correct. However, his newly formed body is still stabilizing. We should give him some time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Incredible work, Albedo.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I graciously accept the compliment. Mm... It really is rather remarkable, what we've accomplished.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, how do you feel right now?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Quite good. I did what I set out to do, and achieved a personal goal.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I think even she would have made a rare facial expression, had she seen it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "She"?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: My master and mother, "Gold" Rhinedottir.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: A long time ago, she sent me to Mondstadt, with the instruction to complete a task of monumental importance: to find the truth of the world.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I had a theory about what she meant, and in time, I was able to corroborate it. Sure enough, "finding the truth of the world" basically stood for "getting a life."

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: That might be easy for most people. But for someone like me, it meant doing a lot of learning about a lot of things.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I had to find out about myself and the world around me. Get to know me, and get to know other people.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: "Life" is the space that exists between me and the world. To become truly human, I had to inhabit that space.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: So, for an artificial human, finding a life is, in some sense, equivalent to finding the truth of the world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's what she meant, huh? Well, no wonder those monsters wanted to infiltrate the city and replace you. They wanted your life for themselves!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Being alive is just existing, but having a life is what makes you truly human. I think that's the message she wanted to get across to me.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Still, I've found this whole series of events has given me new inspiration.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Becoming human is only the beginning. What follows is the choices a human has to make in life, as well as the kinds of family bonds they will form.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Most people would probably see the events of the last few days as something out of a nightmare. But for me, it's just part of my family life.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I fear that the carefree existence my brother has enjoyed thus far will now come to an end. Just like me, he will have to step into the world and face the same constraints as everyone else.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've got an unusual family, that's for sure...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Well, I suppose we get it from our mother. She's highly unusual.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: There are all kinds of families in the world. Some base their life around the family store, others around the farm.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: In my family, I suppose we tend to the flower beds. And now, I'm a gardener, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: As long as you feel like you've gained something from the experience.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Master never showed her face, but if the Hexenzirkel knows what I've done, that means she knows as well and gave her approval.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Since devouring Naberius, it would seem she has finally found a modicum of peace.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: And if so, then I am truly happy for her. She didn't always have a penchant for madness, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Devouring Naberius? What's Naberius?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's the name of the Ruler of Life.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Aunt Alice told me about it not too long ago. But, it came as no surprise. I knew Master would do it sooner or later.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: As for the "Ruler of Life," all I truly know is this: Naberius is not gone. Instead, because of Master's actions, she and Naberius are now one.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: In any case, thank you so much for your help during this ordeal and for choosing to stand by my side through it all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! That's what friends are for!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon took the words right out of my mouth.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hearing you say that means more than I can say.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'll make sure to pass along the sentiment when I report back to Master Jean.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you're heading back to headquarters? Well, good luck with the report!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Thank you. I'll get going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, this Windblume Festival turned out to be a special one. It feels like we really made a difference!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon almost forgot! If the Windblume Star has already been chosen, what is this year's Windblume gonna be?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hmm, wanna take a guess?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Venti! You're back!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Haha, well I couldn't keep my two dear friends in the dark about this year's Windblume, now could I? What do you think of... The Cecilia?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: "The true feelings of the prodigal son." A sentiment as sweet and warm as a gentle spring breeze — perfect for the season!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, give me your hand.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The mages are very pleased that you and Albedo managed to pass their trial. Albedo received the materials he sought, so you deserve something in return as well.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The Hexenzirkel wants you to have this. It contains something entirely one of a kind — a secret of sorts. When the time is right, it will reveal itself to you. So, no need to open it right away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, a gift and a mystery all in one. The mages sure love their secrets, huh...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: According to the sender, you are probably the only person who could make use of something like this, so I suppose it belongs with you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Alright, thanks.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ah, well, all I did was deliver it. Although, I did go to great lengths during this whole ordeal. I suppose a reward for my efforts wouldn't be out of the question...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've helped a lot, Venti! How about we treat you to a drink?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Really? I'll hold you to that, you know! No going back on your word!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course not! Let's go to the tavern right now!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Haha, music to my ears! I'm so happy I could fly! It's like this festival was made for me or something...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: "When no love remains for the songs to tell, the world becomes naught but an empty shell..."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: "Cruel is said fate, cruel it may be, were it not for a hero who could set us all free."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: "Through shadows so cold, he sought wisdom untold, chasing a fragrance, the wind only knows."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: "Thus wistfulness waned and faded into night, as he stepped from the darkness, and into the light."

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Let's call it a day here. Thank you for accompanying me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pleasure! We sure learned a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Mondstadt's a lively place during the Windblume Festival. You should take a look around, and pick out some nice souvenirs for yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah, the festival! Wonder who the Windblume Star's gonna be this time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Well, we've been too busy dealing with this situation the entire time. Who else would be free to work during the Windblume Festival?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'm sure we'll find out on the day of.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: As you all know, during this year's Windblume Festival, the people of Mondstadt have banded together to defeat several waves of monsters that tried to invade our city.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Accordingly, we would like to award the title of Windblume Star to someone who made an outstanding contribution to the defense operation.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: This is someone who may not look like a strong warrior, but whose keen insights played a vital role in gaining control over the conflict. His words and songs always have a way of lifting people's spirits, and they were a great support to us all.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Let's give a round of applause to this year's Windblume Star — Venti the bard!

dialogues.speaker: Audience
dialogues.text: Woooooo! Yay, Venti!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Huh? No way, you're really gonna pick me?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Why not? You're the perfect person for the job.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hmm... Alright. Does that mean I get unlimited free drinks at the tavern?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I'm sure they'll be more than happy to support this year's Windblume Star. If you'd like, you can even take a drink while you give your acceptance speech to the crowd.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ahaha... In that case — instead of a speech, how about a song?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Everyone, the best bard in the land is about to begin his performance. So don't go away! Gather round, and lend me your ears!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Before we set out, there's someone you need to meet.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Head to my office. He's waiting for you there.

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: I'm feeling a little nervous, but also kind of excited... It's a strange feeling. I've never felt anything like it.

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: But don't worry, I can cope! I gotta do my best to stay in a good frame of mind, so that Albedo's plan can succeed.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Nice to have you back safe and sound. Now, time to relax and switch off — you've earned it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, this place is as freezing as ever... *whimper* Paimon's hands are turning to ice...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Want to climb into my hood?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sure? Is it warm in there?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It should take the edge off, and it might improve your mood. But I recommend finding a heat source for a more potent effect.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Windblume Festival is about to begin! Let's go check it out!
